draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Assagao! This hill-ringed village 4 km west of Mapusa is called the 'Land of Flowers'. People also call it the 'Artist's village', 'Goa's Tuscany' and even 'The Beverly Hills of Goa'.
draft.hungryLine: Assagao is more village lanes than restaurant row, so ask around for home-style Goan cooking.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Wander 9 minutes to neighbouring Ponolem, or walk about 20 minutes to St. Michael's Church in Anjuna, one of Goa's oldest standing churches.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Take the leafy road that heads downhill past St. Cajetan Church towards Anjuna, the beaches of Anjuna and Vagator lie just west.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Long before the Portuguese, Assagao's early residents were Saraswat Brahmins of the Atri gotra, and Ravalnath was the village's presiding deity.

spots.name: Ponolem
spots.detail: 9 min walk · A small neighbouring Bardez village

spots.name: St. Michael's Church
spots.detail: 20 min walk · Built in 1613, one of the oldest churches still standing in Goa

legends.title: Zagor, the night vigil
legends.body: Next door in Siolim, people celebrate Zagor, a nocturnal vigil. It's a festival of dance, drama and music that runs through the night.

tips.title: Pick the right fork.
tips.body: Coming from Mapusa the road splits in two, one way runs past St. Cajetan Church to Anjuna and the other past the Panchayat Office to Badem.

tips.title: Skip museums on Mondays.
tips.body: The Houses of Goa Museum elsewhere in Bardez opens Tuesday to Sunday.

story.title: Ravalnath's village
story.body: Assagao's early inhabitants were Saraswat Brahmins of the Atri gotra. All were Hindu, with Ravalnath as the presiding deity.

story.title: Under Portuguese rule
story.body: Like the rest of Goa, Assagao was long held by the Portuguese. Churches like St. Cajetan's still mark the village roads.

story.title: A village of schools
story.body: Assagao grew into an education hub. It's home to Agnel Institute of Technology and Design, DMC College and Assagao Union High School.

story.title: Land of Flowers
story.body: Today Assagao wears many nicknames, from 'Land of Flowers' to 'Goa's Tuscany'. Football and cricket are the village's favourite games.
